title: Kushti earth-pit wrestling
summary: Wrestling in a dug and softened earth pit, a tradition of training halls across South Asia. Read your rival, win the grip, and bring him down until both shoulders are pressed to the earth.
howToPlay: Watch the rival's stance: it shows the move he is about to try, and he sometimes feints.
Pick the move that beats it and tap it while the marker crosses the bright zone.
Win the hold first: the big throws need a firm grip and a rival who is already off balance.
Empty his balance bar and he goes down for the pin. Take two of three rounds.
rules: A pin ends the round at once; if time runs out, the wrestler with more points wins it.
Hip throws and body flips only work fully on a rival whose balance is low.
Tapping again while a move is still playing out only tires you.
Only throws, holds and pins are used; there are no strikes.
heritageNote: Kushti, also called pehlwani, is wrestled on an earth floor that is dug, mixed with oil and buttermilk and kept soft. Wrestlers live and train in a school called an akhara under a teacher, with long daily exercise and a careful diet. It grew over centuries in the Indian subcontinent from older local wrestling and Persian styles.
